summary: Build practical skills for heat, flood and drought risk assessment, worker protection and continuity planning. Enquire about this five-day course.
lede: Climate-resilient occupational health and safety management helps HSE managers, occupational-health practitioners and facilities leaders assess climate threats to workers and operations. Learners practise mapping heat, flood and drought risks, assessing worker vulnerability, developing heat-action plans and setting emergency triggers for continuity; climate projections and automated analytics receive an applied introduction.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who must connect climate hazards with worker protection, site controls, emergency readiness and operational continuity.
modules: Heat Stress Controls and Action Plans
prerequisites: Working knowledge of occupational health and safety processes is recommended. Experience with incident reporting, site inspections, emergency planning or workforce welfare will help you apply the exercises. No coding or programming is required. Climate modelling is taught at conceptual and operational application levels, while risk assessment, action planning and reporting receive hands-on treatment. You should bring a laptop if possible; provided templates can also support paper-based delivery.
